question: How fast does a fist sized rock hit the ground after falling off a 300 m cliff?
headline: Hits the ground 8.72 s after release at 56.8 m/s (205 km/h). Without air it would land after 7.82 s at 76.7 m/s, so drag takes 26% off the impact speed.
confidence_reasons: passed step convergence, hand calculation, vacuum drop, energy balance, units and sanity

checks.name: step convergence
checks.summary: flown again with a tolerance ten times tighter, the flight time 8.72 s and impact speed 56.8 m/s moved by at most 1e-06% (the impact speed)

checks.name: hand calculation
checks.summary: with the air at its density halfway down (1.207 kg/m3) the terminal speed is 66.2 m/s, and v = vt tanh(g t / vt) with h = vt^2/g ln cosh(g t / vt) gives 8.719 s and 56.9 m/s against 8.717 s and 56.8 m/s from the run (0.16% apart), the difference coming from the air thickening on the way down

checks.name: vacuum drop
checks.summary: with the air taken away and gravity held at its ground value the run lands after 7.822 s at 76.7 m/s, and sqrt(2h/g) gives 7.822 s and 76.7 m/s (1.5e-13% apart). The air adds 0.895 s to the fall and takes 19.9 m/s off the impact

checks.name: energy balance
checks.summary: drag took 1.37 kJ and gravity gave 3.03 kJ, which leaves 1.66 kJ of kinetic energy at impact, and the impact speed carries 1.66 kJ (apart by 4.9e-07% of the largest term)

checks.name: units and sanity
checks.summary: speeds stay under Mach 0.167, 1.03 kg in a 9 cm body, 2700 kg/m3 for a sphere

assumptions: A point mass in a vertical plane, so it does not spin, tumble or move sideways, and its drag acts against the air rushing past it.
Drag coefficient 0.6 on a frontal area 9 cm across, the same at every speed.
The 1976 US standard atmosphere from 0 m above sea level, a standard day.
Gravity falls off with the square of the distance to the Earth's center, over a flat Earth that does not rotate.

_figures: Altitude and speed over the flight, by phase

notes: A solid sphere 9 cm across, so 1.031 kg.
